milestones.title: One usable server per checkout starts, attaches, stops and reports its state without races or hidden kills
milestones.problem: The shared server's election is sound at the create step (O_CREAT|O_EXCL at apps/majordomus-cli/src/lease.rs:516-520, proved by apps/majordomus-cli/tests/mcp_shared.rs::a_storm_of_clients_converges_on_one_server_and_one_board and case 191), but what follows it is not. The lease probe is GET / on the same four workers that run tool calls (apps/majordomus-cli/src/lease.rs:896-925, apps/majordomus-cli/src/http/server.rs:23), so four long calls make a healthy server look dead and a new client takes it over. A server that lost its lease keeps its bridged sessions forever, because bridges ping every 20 s (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mcp/bridge.rs:19) and the serve loop counts them as attached (apps/majordomus-cli/src/commands/serve.rs:136-146). `serve stop` is a SIGTERM whose handler unlinks the lease unconditionally and re-raises (apps/majordomus-cli/src/lease.rs:1164-1212), so it can delete a successor's lease and never runs the ordered stop (apps/majordomus-cli/src/shared.rs:282-289). The lease timings the policy declares never reach the mcp and serve elections (apps/majordomus-cli/src/lease.rs:89-191 OnceLock filled before apps/majordomus-cli/src/policy.rs:364 runs). Lifecycle state is an observer's reading of a file (apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/builtin/server.rs:163-177) with no degraded, stopping or failed, and the live server of 2026-10-09 had logged nothing for eight hours because it inherited MAJORDOMUS_LOG=error (apps/majordomus-cli/src/commands/serve.rs:727-729). A UI-first server stops after 900 s while being viewed, because only MCP sessions count as use (apps/majordomus-cli/src/shared.rs:250-253). Measured in the runtime baseline audit of 2026-10-09 at master 1fb8d6be44 (plan/RUNTIME_BASELINE.md).
milestones.outcome: Entering a checkout, opening the Cockpit, or starting any number of MCP clients converges on one server for that checkout, which is taken over only when it is dead, stops in order when asked, removes only its own lease, reports a typed state every surface reads, and stays up while any surface uses it.
milestones.current_state: Implemented and tested: atomic create, a published URL only after the socket serves (apps/majordomus-cli/src/shared.rs:294-305), stale, corrupt, abandoned, busy and superseded leases, port fallback, stdio hygiene. Partial: the probe, takeover and publish are compare-then-act (apps/majordomus-cli/src/lease.rs:778-798, 1082-1107); a lost server's existing sessions are served indefinitely (apps/majordomus-cli/src/http/mcp.rs:113-118); SIGTERM is not graceful (apps/majordomus-cli/tests/mcp_shared.rs::sigterm_removes_the_lease_before_the_process_dies asserts signal 15); declared timings are dead in mcp and serve. Absent: degraded, stopping and failed states, and liveness from non-MCP use. Refuted premises of the pack: there is no `majordomus ui` command, `serve ensure` and `env enter` are the UI-first entries (apps/majordomus-cli/src/commands/serve.rs:481-576, apps/majordomus-cli/src/commands/env.rs:701-760); `serve ensure` and `serve stop` are CLI-only by stated design and not capabilities; apps/majordomus-cli/src/served.rs is deployment observation, not server lifecycle; the top-level `majordomus doctor` is a governance doctor (lib/doctor.sh:53-77) and checks nothing about the server. The launcher rebuilding the executable in the primary checkout is I2059.
milestones.desired_state: Every lifecycle fault in the audit's matrix has a test: N concurrent first clients, a busy owner, a killed owner, a lost lease with live bridges, a SIGTERM racing a takeover, a declared timing, a UI-only user. server.status answers one of absent, starting, ready, degraded, outdated, stale, stopping or failed, decided in one function. docs/MCP.md and README.md describe the server that ships: one per checkout, what it writes, when it ends.
non_scope: A `majordomus ui` command, unless I2131's record decides one is needed beyond `serve ensure`.
One server for all repositories. ADR 0044 decided one per checkout and the board is gathered across them.
Graceful termination inside the production container, which is I0906 (fly-deployment).
The bridge's resend of a tool call, which is I2145 (mcp-transports-are-reliable).
acceptance_criteria: A server whose four workers are busy with tool calls is never taken over by a client that started meanwhile
A server that lost its lease has no session left after a declared grace and exits by itself
No process removes a lease file whose token is not its own, proved under a SIGTERM racing a takeover
`serve stop` runs the ordered stop and leaves no open episode
A lease timing declared in policy.yaml is the one the mcp and serve elections wait
server.status reports stopping, failed and degraded, each from a test that produces the state
A server used only through the Cockpit or /events is not stopped as idle
validation: cargo test --test mcp_shared --test serve_lifecycle --test lease_busy --test lease_lost --test lease_declared --test server_status
risks: Every issue here edits apps/majordomus-cli/src/lease.rs, apps/majordomus-cli/src/shared.rs or apps/majordomus-cli/src/commands/serve.rs, so they are not parallel-safe with each other; one worker should carry them in dependency order.
A wrong takeover rule turns one healthy server into two. Each change needs the storm test (apps/majordomus-cli/tests/mcp_shared.rs) green before and after.
The live servers on the owner's machine run whatever was last built; a change to the lease schema reaches them only on restart, so a mixed fleet must be tolerated during the rollout.

milestones.title: A runtime is safe to reach from another machine, and joining the mesh trusts nobody by accident
milestones.problem: The runtime pack's baseline audit (2026-10-09, M01) read the server and the mesh against their documents and found the security model held only on the network hop. A server bound beyond loopback accepted every state-changing request from any host that sent no Origin header: plan transitions, continuity writes, any capability through executions.start, and mesh sessions, claims, handovers and reviews that the node then signed with its own trusted key. Three servers on the owner's machine were bound that way at the time. Beside it: reloading the journal skips the trust check, so a revoked key's events return on restart; Lamport stamps are not bounded, so a trusted key can backdate a claim to win every conflict; an expired claim revives and wins after a partition; hello messages name no recipient; trust is read from the branch's working tree; discovery inputs have unbounded channels and reply reads.
milestones.outcome: Discovery is not trust, trust is not authorization, and a caller is admitted to change anything only by a key the trust policy names. A host that can reach a runtime reads it and changes nothing it cannot authenticate; every event in the journal was checked against the trust policy that holds now, whether it arrived over a link or from disk; and the limits the documents state are the limits the code enforces.
milestones.current_state: Remote state-changing requests were admitted by address alone (fixed by I2123). The journal reload, Lamport bounds, claim revival, hello recipient, trust-root and unbounded-input findings stand as recorded in the audit.
milestones.desired_state: Every threat in docs/MESH.md's security model names the test that defends it, and every finding of the baseline audit's threat list is either defended with a test or recorded as a limitation the documents state.
non_scope: Encrypting the transport. ADR 0032 decided no TLS dependency; confidentiality stays the network's.
Accounts or a login. A remote writer, when one is needed, is admitted by a key the trust policy names.
acceptance_criteria: A request from an address that is not loopback runs only a capability that reads or whose input is a signed message, on every transport that knows the caller's address
Every event the journal holds passed the trust policy in force, whether it arrived over a link or was reloaded from disk
A trusted key cannot order its claim before claims already admitted, and an expired claim does not return as live
Every bound the security model names is enforced on the input it names, with a test that sends one more
risks: A remote MCP client loses writes it used to have (announce, mesh sessions). The route that remains is a tunnel that ends on loopback.

milestones.title: Every mesh node follows the published release by itself, versions meet safely, and a release's provenance can be checked
milestones.problem: The pack assumes a self-updater and signed releases. Both premises are refuted. `majordomus update` regenerates provider projections from policy (lib/update.sh:4); there is no self-update command, and docs/DISTRIBUTION.md:416-439 says so; to upgrade, a person reruns install.sh with --version. Artifacts are checksummed, not signed: sha256 and size in releases/<tag>.json are checked by site/static/install.sh:478 (called at :706), and docs/DISTRIBUTION.md:151-153 defers signing on purpose. What exists is compatibility risk: the superseded check covers only a binary replaced at the same path (apps/majordomus-cli/src/lease.rs:695-709), while the installer uses one directory per version, so a new client attaches to an older server and only an Outdated warning records it (apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/builtin/server.rs:410-424). version-surface prices the public surface only; mesh discovery and link versions (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/protocol.rs:36-40, apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/link.rs:50-53), the lease schema and journal events are outside it. Measured in the runtime baseline audit of 2026-10-09 at master 1fb8d6be44 (plan/RUNTIME_BASELINE.md).
milestones.outcome: An enrolled mesh node follows the stable release by itself through the one installer, forward only, activating in order and rolling back a failed activation (ADR 0161); a newer client replaces an older server in an ordered hand-off and an older client is told it is older; a change to any wire or on-disk schema needs a version bump; a released archive carries a provenance attestation the installer checks.
milestones.current_state: Implemented: install.sh verifies checksum and size, refuses traversal and non-HTTPS; release-verdict gates the release on CI; version-surface covers capabilities, routes, tools, commands and schemas; MCP protocol negotiation. Absent: a reader of the stable pointer on any node (every node is upgraded by hand), cross-path version hand-off, wire-schema pricing, a v1 advertisement fixture, provenance.
milestones.desired_state: The compatibility matrix in plan/RUNTIME_BASELINE.md lists adjacent client/server and mesh versions with a test for each pair, and docs/DISTRIBUTION.md states what each install path verifies. The owner decided on 2026-10-14 that a background update check is wanted (ADR 0161): every enrolled node follows releases/latest.json through self update, which re-runs install.sh, and the mesh shows each node's version (I2720-I2724).
non_scope: A second installer or updater; install.sh stays the one path (pack M11), and self update re-runs it (ADR 0161).
A network fetch on entering a repository.
Restarting a client's server while it has work in flight; hand-off goes through I2127's session move.
acceptance_criteria: An enrolled, following node is on the version releases/latest.json names within one check interval of a release, with no person on it
A failed activation rolls back to the previous version by itself and the board names node, version and failed check
A client of version N+1 beside a server of version N at another path ends with one server of N+1 and no lost session
A wire or lease or journal schema change without a version bump fails version-surface
Each release archive carries an attestation that verifies for this repository
risks: A hand-off between versions depends on the old server ending its sessions (I2127); landing I2163 first would strand clients on the old server.
Following automatically raises the cost of a bad archive; I2165 (attestation) is raised to p1 with ADR 0161.
Attestation needs repository permissions in the publish job; the release workflow's permissions block changes with it.

milestones.title: Shared policy across repositories and workers
milestones.problem: Policy is per repository. An organisation running many repositories has no way to state a rule once, and no way to see where it is not being followed.
milestones.outcome: A policy can be shared across repositories and workers, with local override remaining explicit and drift from the shared source detectable in one command.
milestones.current_state: Not started. Everything the tool does today is scoped to a single checkout.
milestones.desired_state: One policy statement governs many repositories, and every deviation from it is visible rather than assumed.
non_scope: A hosted service, a registry, or any component that must be running for the tool to work
acceptance_criteria: A shared policy can be consumed by more than one repository without copying it
A local override is explicit and survives an update of the shared source
Drift between the shared policy and a repository's effective policy is reported by one command
risks: Shared policy is where a local tool becomes a distributed one; the offline guarantee has to survive it.

milestones.title: Every surface projects the same state, says when it was observed, and keeps no list of its own
milestones.problem: The core projection holds: the live server's 181 /api/v1 routes equal the 181 OpenAPI operations, which equal the committed docs/generated/openapi.json, and the executor is the only dispatch path (apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/executor.rs:156). Around it: freshness is not uniform, since dashboard/overview, episodes, lifecycle/runtime, plan/status, served and mesh carry no observed_at, the overview badge is permanently stale on an idle repository (apps/majordomus-cli/src/index.rs:44, apps/majordomus-cli/src/live.rs:250-252) and GET / said stale: null while serving a build 12 commits behind HEAD. The parity property compares HTTP only for GET routes and excludes the coordination read models (apps/majordomus-cli/tests/properties.rs:166-168,300), and nothing compares CLI JSON with HTTP. /swagger has no CSP and no SRI on the same origin as the write routes (apps/majordomus-cli/src/http/swagger.rs:52,79). The Cockpit and the site keep at least nine consumer-side catalogues of what the registry declares, and ADR 0004 says nothing has a second registry. Measured in the runtime baseline audit of 2026-10-09 at master 1fb8d6be44 (plan/RUNTIME_BASELINE.md).
milestones.outcome: A reader on any surface sees the same value, the time it was observed and whether it is stale; a capability added to or removed from the registry appears or disappears everywhere with no consumer edit; a page served beside the write routes runs only script it shipped.
milestones.current_state: Implemented: routes, OpenAPI, MCP and the generated registry dataset are registry-derived and drift-checked. Partial: freshness, parity, Cockpit data access (five pages read ctx.registry directly, .ai/repo/ui-integrity-baseline.txt:9-13). Second registries: the clap tree (checked both ways by apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/closure.rs), cli/local.rs LOCAL (89 commands), native web surfaces (apps/majordomus-cli/src/web/discover.rs:150), Cockpit routes (three lists, cross-checked), and the consumer copies listed in plan/RUNTIME_BASELINE.md.
milestones.desired_state: Every state-reporting answer carries observed_at and source, enforced over the registry; the parity property covers writers and the CLI; no Cockpit or site file names a value an enum, a capability or HttpExposure already declares; /swagger and every GET refuse what a hostile page or rebinding host could do.
non_scope: Removing the clap tree or cli/local.rs LOCAL; both are measured second declarations (SURFACES F-1, F-4) and this milestone records them rather than rewriting the CLI.
Writing a static site that claims live state; the site stays a picture labelled as one.
Reporting a replaced executable, which is I1502.
acceptance_criteria: A test over the registry fails when a state-reporting capability answers without observed_at
The parity test covers every capability with an HTTP route and every capability with a CLI path
GET /swagger answers with a CSP and integrity hashes, and a foreign Host is refused on GET
A gate fails on a literal /api/v1/ path or a copied enum value in Cockpit or site code
validation: cargo test --test properties --test projections --test dashboard --test http_serve --test http_host
risks: Adding observed_at to capability outputs changes their schemas and so the public surface; version-surface will price it as a change, which is correct.
Extending parity to POST routes runs writers in tests; each must run against a synthetic repository, never the checkout.

milestones.title: Every verifiable claim and widget resolves to revision-bound test evidence, on every surface
milestones.problem: Claims bind to tests by path, and only `majordomus evidence show` asks whether a claim is proven, always at the working tree of whoever runs it. The site cannot ask that question about the commit it was built from, and no widget on it names the subject that would prove what it shows: where a page says verified, the word was placed by hand. CI runs the suite and the crate tests on every merge and keeps none of it in the ledger. A test that declined to run reads `failing`, while a case that declines by exiting zero is recorded as a pass. The rules module holds a second copy of the freshness derivation, the entry preflight proposed in PR #578 counts a run as current by a filter of its own with no containment test, and ADR 0068 and ADR 0080 disagree about where CI evidence goes. Each surface that wants to say verified derives it differently or not at all.
milestones.outcome: Evidence is indexed by subject and judged at the presented revision, as ADR 0087 records. Every claim, rule, feature, command, capability, MCP tool and use case is a subject of one derived index, and every widget that states behaviour names one. Every surface reads its verdict from the tracked ledger alone, through one freshness function and one aggregation, at the revision it presents: the CLI and HTTP and MCP at the working tree or the checked-out commit, the site at the commit it was built from. A trunk run reaches the ledger through a reviewed recording pull request, and a supplementary record (a run record, coverage, a local row) can only weaken a verdict, naming itself when it does. Verified is rendered only for the one proven row of the freshness table, on every surface.
milestones.current_state: On master at 5a0770c437 the tracked ledger holds local recordings only, and how many claims reach each state is what `majordomus evidence show --format json | jq .totals` prints. There is no subject index; the command-to-test join is derived in shell more than once (`scripts/generate-site-data`, `lib/commands.sh`, `scripts/ci/command-furnished`). `rules/mod.rs` carries its own `changed_since` and its own state mapping beside `evidence/mod.rs`. The decisions this milestone builds on are proposed and unlanded: ADR 0068 on PR #577 (CI evidence as an artifact and a published dataset), ADR 0080 on PR #629 (the recording branch, and the skip word), ADR 0071 on PR #600 (delivery dimensions, with a private containment implementation); PR #597 adds the rules corpus verdict and PR #578 the entry preflight.
milestones.desired_state: A reader of any page of the site follows a widget's badge to the evidence of its subject and sees the verdict at the commit the page was built from, with the run that produced it and every record that weakened it. `majordomus evidence subject <key>` answers the same question from a terminal, over HTTP and over MCP, and the Cockpit shows the same verdict. A merge to master is followed by a recording pull request that lands its run's executions in the ledger. A claim then reads `proven` at a trunk commit that nothing but ledger-only commits separates from the recorded one, and `inputs_unchanged` or `stale`, naming what changed, where other merges landed in between; whether the process makes the first the rule is the owner's decision (ADR 0087, Consequences). A skipped test reads `not_run` with its reason, and no surface anywhere reads greener than the ledger for the revision it presents.
non_scope: Accepting ADR 0041, 0068, 0080 or 0087; acceptance is the owner's act
Bumping the version; a pull request that moves the public surface inherits the version already on master by merging it
Judging a commit other than the checked-out one or the site's build commit
MCP resource templates per subject; evidence is reached through tool calls
Making the required `ci` check depend on the evidence job
New shell automation (ADR 0069)
A regex crate or any other new dependency for the redactor
Stamping use-case evidence with a commit in the committed catalogue
acceptance_criteria: Model: one freshness function, one presented revision, one containment and one aggregation judge every verdict, a skip reads `not_run`, and one derived index names every subject; proven by test/cases/502_evidence_is_judged_at_the_presented_revision.sh, test/cases/507_evidence_subjects_are_derived.sh and test/cases/501_verdict_words_are_status_words.sh

Producer: every recorded run carries the commit and tree it measured, a crate binary that ran nothing is a skip, CI's report is the tracked ledger's verdict derived before the run records, and a trunk run reaches the ledger through one recording pull request, stopping at a commit the ledger covers and recording a ledger-only commit over an unrecorded merge; proven by test/cases/505_a_recording_carries_what_its_run_measured.sh, test/cases/506_a_crate_binary_that_ran_nothing_is_not_a_pass.sh, test/cases/357_ci_records_evidence.sh, test/cases/510_ci_evidence_reaches_the_ledger_through_a_recording_branch.sh and test/cases/511_every_runner_report_carries_its_revision_and_reason.sh

Surfaces: the CLI, HTTP, MCP, the Cockpit and the entry preflight answer by subject from the one authority, and a supplementary record only weakens; proven by test/cases/508_evidence_answers_by_subject.sh, test/cases/509_supplementary_records_only_weaken.sh, test/cases/513_cockpit_shows_evidence.sh, test/cases/514_every_test_line_is_read.sh, test/cases/515_a_local_run_stays_local.sh and test/cases/529_the_preflight_reads_the_one_verdict.sh

Site: every widget names its subject, every subject has an evidence route, the publication is bound to its build and allow-listed, and published text is redacted once; proven by test/cases/504_public_text_is_redacted_once.sh, test/cases/512_evidence_publication_is_a_projection.sh, test/cases/516_evidence_routes_render_from_the_subject_index.sh, test/cases/517_a_panel_subject_is_joined_from_its_route.sh, test/cases/518_evidence_publication_is_bound_to_its_build.sh and test/cases/520_every_widget_names_its_proof.sh

Policy: subject findings refuse, the evidence baseline is rewritten in the same change, and the validator reads every widget; proven by test/cases/522_evidence_check_reads_widgets.sh and test/cases/523_evidence_rules_are_gated.sh

Tests: no surface is greener than the ledger, the badge works in a browser at phone width, tampered evidence is refused, and coverage is shown with its commit; proven by test/cases/524_no_surface_is_greener_than_the_ledger.sh, test/cases/525_an_evidence_badge_works_in_a_browser.sh, test/cases/526_tampered_evidence_is_refused.sh and test/cases/527_coverage_is_shown_with_its_commit.sh
Docs: the evidence reference names what the code declares and is held to the tree; proven by test/cases/528_the_evidence_reference_is_held_to_the_tree.sh

Deploy: a deploy verifies the evidence routes it publishes, and the evidence survives artifact expiry on gh-pages; proven by test/cases/521_deploy_verifies_evidence_routes.sh, test/cases/519_evidence_survives_artifact_expiry.sh and the live page https://majordomus.dev/evidence/
risks: Until the recording branch runs, the tracked ledger holds only local rows and the site renders mostly `not_run`. That is the true state; the badges follow the CI wiring for that reason.
The decisions this milestone builds on are proposed on open pull requests (#577, #578, #597, #600, #629). A slice stacked on one of them waits for it, and the landing order is the owner's.

`proven` at a trunk revision needs a quiet trunk: a recording costs a full suite run and then the required checks, and a code merge landing in that window leaves claims `inputs_unchanged` or `stale` at the landing commit. Until the owner decides whether the process makes `proven` reachable or `required_tests_current` binds to a reachable state, on a busy trunk the delivery dimension rarely passes and the site rarely renders verified (ADR 0087, Consequences).
The recording pull request needs a token whose events start the required workflow. Until the owner chooses between dispatching validate.yml and an App token, the CI wiring slice cannot land.
Every landing makes the open slices' pull requests conflict on derived files; each is refreshed by merging master with the derived merge driver, never by a rebase.

milestones.title: The mesh works out of the box: trusted machines find each other by every means and their sessions cooperate from the first turn
milestones.problem: On 2026-10-10 the owner called mesh cooperation tragic and ordered it to work out of the box, by every discovery means, from the moment an LLM client, the MCP server or `majordomus serve` starts. A read of the code found six gaps that no existing milestone covers: no Tailscale discovery (the tailnet is reached only through 100.x addresses hand-written in .ai/repo/mesh/majordomus.yaml); a server binds and advertises 127.0.0.1 unless told otherwise, so two machines on default settings never dial each other (apps/majordomus-cli/src/cli.rs:3355-3362, mesh/address.rs:39-45); `majordomus init` ships no mesh declaration, so a fresh repository has no mesh at all; a linked worktree with no server of its own has no cooperation (`mesh handover publish` answered 'cooperation inactive'); mesh.state and mesh.peers return 56-134 kB with no filter; and a review request has no body, cannot be closed and never expires.
milestones.outcome: A trusted machine that starts any Majordomus surface in a repository with the mesh declared is linked to every other trusted machine on the LAN or tailnet without a hand-written address, every worktree takes part, and what the mesh holds can be read in one tool answer.
milestones.current_state: Multicast on one LAN segment and five hand-written rendezvous hubs; loopback-bound servers; no declaration in a fresh repository; worktrees and review requests outside the loop.
milestones.desired_state: Tailscale, multicast, broadcast and rendezvous discovery; a mesh-enabled server reachable on the tailnet and LAN under the trust list; init that declares the mesh and enrols the machine's key; worktrees that cooperate through the primary's runtime; bounded, filterable mesh reads; a review lifecycle that ends.
non_scope: Trusting a machine nobody listed: runtime-trust (I2261) keeps an unlisted clone off the mesh, and nothing here weakens it.
Session start, briefing and Codex/Gemini participation: every-session-joins-the-mesh (I2285-I2292).
Assigning and executing work on a peer: mesh-peers-execute-assigned-work (I2332-I2336).
acceptance_criteria: Two trusted machines on one tailnet, each with a fresh `majordomus init` plus enrolment, link with no address written by hand
A server whose mesh is enabled is reachable from a trusted peer on the tailnet and refuses an untrusted one
A worktree of a checkout whose primary runs a server publishes a handover and a claim
mesh.state and mesh.peers answer a filtered summary under 16 kB
A review request carries a body, and can be withdrawn or expire
risks: It builds on runtime-trust and on I2123 (PR #860), which are not on master yet: I2411 lands after them.
Binding beyond loopback widens what can reach a server: it waits for the remote-caller restrictions of runtime-trust (I2123, #860) and is refused for a node the trust list does not name.

milestones.title: A repository that adopts Majordomus gains two directories and two lines, and can give them back
milestones.problem: What Majordomus leaves in a repository it adopts is not decided anywhere; it is the sum of what each subsystem happened to write. Provider files at the root, scripts, configuration beside configuration, generated registries that became inputs, and no record of which of them Majordomus put there. The costs compound in three directions at once. A person cannot tell what is theirs and what is the tool's, so nothing can be safely removed. A second provider means a second copy of the same instructions rather than a second adapter. And every subsystem rediscovers the repository for itself — the CLI, the environment entry, the documentation, the server — so the same facts are read four ways and disagree on the fourth.
milestones.outcome: Adoption is a reconciliation, not a template copy. One typed repository model is discovered once and every consumer reads it. A desired integration is computed from that model, diffed against what the repository actually holds, and applied as the smallest mutation that closes the gap — with everything Majordomus owns living under `.ai/` and `.majordomus/`, and anything outside those two namespaces reduced to a small managed bridge whose ownership is recorded. Running the reconciliation twice changes nothing the second time, and uninstalling gives back exactly what was taken and nothing a person authored.
milestones.current_state: `.ai/` and `.majordomus/` both exist and carry real material, and directory contracts are already enforced under `.ai/` (ADR 0011). Against that: provider bootstraps are generated to the root, the environment entry and the CLI each discover the repository their own way, `init` writes what it was written to write rather than what the repository lacks, no ledger records what was placed outside the two namespaces, and nothing can undo an adoption.
milestones.desired_state: `majordomus init` on a foreign repository adds `.ai/`, `.majordomus/`, a managed block in `AGENTS.md` and — when direnv is wanted — one stable line in `.envrc`. A second run reports no change. `majordomus uninstall` removes what the ledger records and leaves authored knowledge alone. Adding a valid artifact under a discoverable namespace registers it everywhere, and no list anywhere enumerates what discovery already finds.
non_scope: A configuration format that restates what the repository can be inspected for
Rewriting a working subsystem for symmetry rather than for a defect
Deleting user-authored content on any path, under any flag, without an explicit and separate instruction
A second worktree convention, a second handover format or a second doctor
Provider-specific semantics anywhere but an adapter
acceptance_criteria: Everything Majordomus persists in an adopted repository lives under `.ai/` or `.majordomus/`, and every exception outside them is a bridge recorded in the ownership ledger
One typed repository model is discovered once per process and every consumer — CLI, environment, API, MCP, Cockpit, documentation, providers, completion — reads that model rather than the filesystem
The desired integration is a value, the plan is a diff against what is there, and the apply is the smallest mutation that closes it
A second `init` on a conforming repository produces no change, proved by a test rather than by observation
`uninstall` reverses every recorded mutation, refuses to touch a bridge a person has edited, and leaves `.ai/` authored content in place by default
Every generated artifact declares its provenance, its generator and the inputs it derives from, and no generated artifact is read back as canonical input
No hand-maintained list enumerates artifacts that discovery finds, and adding a valid artifact registers it in every consumer with no second edit
Environment entry stays local and bounded, with no network and no build, and its cost is measured against a declared budget
Every invariant above is a project rule with a check that CI executes, each proved by a negative test
risks: A reconciler that computes a desired state can also impose one. Everything it would change outside the two namespaces has to be visible in a dry run before it is applied, and a bridge a person edited is a conflict rather than an overwrite.

One repository model is a bottleneck as well as a spine: every consumer that reads it pays its discovery cost. The cost has to be measured against the environment-entry budget before the model becomes mandatory, not after.

Migrating this repository's own footprint is the most dangerous phase, because the tool is being changed by the thing it is changing. The migration runs through the reconciler with a dry run first, never through a move script.

An ownership ledger that drifts from the filesystem is worse than none: it authorises deletions it cannot justify. Every recorded mutation carries the hash it was written with, and a mismatch stops the removal.
Provider adapters invite provider semantics to leak into the model. The test is whether a new provider is an implementation of one trait, or an edit in six places.

milestones.title: The deployed surfaces know who is asking, and the identity providers are data
milestones.problem: Everything this repository serves is served to whoever reaches the port. That was safe while the server bound loopback and the only reader was the person standing in front of the checkout, and it stops being safe the moment the deployment milestone puts a public HTTPS URL in front of the same router: the Cockpit, the API, the OpenAPI document and the MCP surface would all be readable by anyone who found the host, and no mutating capability could ever be exposed through the browser because there would be nobody to attribute the mutation to. The obvious repair is the wrong one twice over. Hand-written provider clients for Google and for Facebook would be two implementations of one flow, and a compiled-in list of which providers exist would put an identity decision in Rust source where every other decision of this repository is a declarative object under .ai/repo/. The provider set is expected to change — both of the first two may be struck and replaced once the audience is known — and a change of that kind must be an edit to one object, not a release of the executable.
milestones.outcome: One canonical identity-provider kind under .ai/repo/identity/providers/ describes each provider as data: its issuer, its endpoints or its discovery document, the scopes requested, the claim that carries a stable subject and the environment variable names its credentials arrive in. A single OpenID-Connect-shaped flow in the executable serves every provider in that directory; Google and Facebook are two objects, not two code paths. Sessions are cookie-borne, signed, short and revocable; identity is attached to a request once, in the router, and every surface — HTTP, Cockpit, OpenAPI, MCP — reads it from the same place. The capability registry's effect classification, not a per-route list, decides what an anonymous reader may do, and the OpenAPI document and the Cockpit both state that decision because both project it from the registry. Striking a provider is deleting one file and regenerating.
milestones.current_state: There is no authentication of any kind: no session, no cookie, no identity type, no login route, no credential handling and no notion of a caller anywhere in apps/majordomus-cli/src/http. The lease file records a URL and the server warns when it binds anything but loopback. The deployment milestone (fly-deployment) states as non-scope that mutating deployment operations must not be exposed to unauthenticated HTTP or to the browser, which is a constraint this milestone is what removes.
milestones.desired_state: A reader who opens the public URL is served the public read-only surfaces as they are today. A reader who signs in with any provider declared in .ai/repo/identity/providers/ gets a session, is named in the Cockpit, and may invoke the capabilities the effect policy allows a signed-in reader to invoke. Adding a third provider is one YAML file; removing the first two is deleting two files; neither is a code change, and the generated documentation, the Cockpit's sign-in offer and the OpenAPI security scheme all follow from the same objects.
non_scope: A user database, a profile store, or any record of a reader beyond the session needed to answer the next request
Passwords, password reset, e-mail verification or any credential this repository would itself have to store
A provider-specific code path, client library or SDK for Google, for Facebook or for any successor
Authorisation roles, groups or an access-control language beyond what the capability registry's effect classification already decides
Any credential, client secret or token committed to the repository, written into a generated artifact, rendered into the site or logged
Exposing mutating capabilities to a signed-in reader before the effect classification says which ones are safe to expose at all
Signing in to the local development server as a requirement; loopback stays open so the existing workflow is unchanged
acceptance_criteria: Every fact about a provider — issuer, endpoints, scopes, subject claim, credential variable names, display name, ordering — lives in one object under .ai/repo/identity/providers/ and nowhere else
Google and Facebook are each one such object, and the executable contains no identifier, endpoint or branch naming either of them
Deleting a provider object removes the provider from the sign-in offer, from the generated documentation, from the OpenAPI security scheme and from the Cockpit, with no other edit

The flow validates state and nonce, rejects a callback whose state it did not issue, pins the session to the issuer and subject, and refuses a provider whose credentials are absent rather than starting a flow that cannot complete
The session cookie is signed, HttpOnly, SameSite-constrained, Secure when the surface is served over HTTPS, and expires; signing out revokes it server-side rather than only clearing it in the browser
Identity is resolved once in the router and read by every surface from that one place; no surface parses the cookie a second time
What an anonymous reader may do is derived from the capability registry's effect classification rather than from a list of routes
No secret sentinel placed in the credential environment variables appears in any response, generated artifact, log line, cache, site output or OpenAPI example
The documentation states how to add a provider and how to remove one, and both statements are executed by a test rather than only written
risks: An OpenID Connect flow written twice — once for the provider that is standards-shaped and once for the one that is not — is the failure this milestone exists to prevent. Facebook's endpoints differ from Google's in their spelling, not in their shape; anything that genuinely cannot be expressed as data about one flow is a defect in the provider object's schema and is fixed there.

Credentials are the one part of this that cannot be data in the repository. The objects name the environment variables; the values arrive from the deployment's secret store and are never read into any structure that is serialised, cached or rendered.
Sign-in invites scope creep towards accounts, profiles and roles. The session exists to answer the next request and nothing more; anything beyond that belongs to a milestone that has a reason for it.
The provider set is expected to be struck. A design that makes Google and Facebook cheap to add but expensive to remove has failed even if it works.

milestones.title: The projection to GitHub is gated, identified and traversable, and a merged pull request leads back to the outcome it served
milestones.problem: This repository already models work once: milestones are outcomes, issues are execution contracts, no status is stored, and `scripts/github-sync` projects both onto GitHub with a hash-marked region that protects what a human wrote. The model is not the defect. The defect is that nothing runs the detector: `core-check` runs `github-sync --plan` and `--render`, never `--check`, so the adapter's exit 11 has never fired in CI. The projection was applied once on 2026-09-04 and has not been applied since. Measured on 2026-09-09 at 867f3a9: 191 drift findings, of which 172 are canonical issues that have never existed on GitHub and 19 are bodies whose canonical text has moved on. All 8 milestones are in sync, which is exactly what makes the rot invisible: the surface a person looks at is the surface that still agrees. Underneath that, the adapter identifies a remote record by parsing its title for an `I0001 — ` prefix and reads the remote through a 200-item page that already holds 19 issues and 117 pull requests, so the mapping breaks when a person renames a title and the read truncates as soon as the backfill runs.
milestones.outcome: The projection cannot rot silently: a gate runs the drift check on every change that can move the model or the adapter, and drift is a CI failure with the record named. Identity travels with the record rather than being parsed out of its title, so renaming a GitHub title moves nothing and creates no duplicate, and the remote can be a fixture, so which record is which is provable with no network. The reconciliation vocabulary distinguishes the states it currently conflates, so `missing` no longer stands for both a record never created and a record a person deleted, and a remote edit is reported as a remote edit. Above the projection, a pull request names the issue it realises and the edge is derived from git and GitHub rather than remembered, so a merged commit leads back to the acceptance criteria it satisfied and an outcome leads forward to the evidence that it holds. The derivations the shell already computes — ready, blocked, waves, next, status — are readable through the same capability surface as every other thing this repository knows, rather than only from a terminal.
milestones.current_state: The canonical model is 15 milestones and 184 issues, validated by `majordomus plan validate` (0 failures, 4 scope warnings) and enforced by `lib/doctor.sh` and `scripts/ci/core-check`. `scripts/github-sync` implements plan, check, apply and render with field ownership and a marker hash. GitHub holds 8 milestones and 19 issues. `--check` exits 11 on drift and no gate calls it. Issues and milestones are served as documents through `objects.get`, and none of the plan's derivations is a capability: `lib/plan.sh` computes them and the Rust executable reads `.ai/repo/project/issues/` for filenames only. Evidence carries an optional `commit` string and no pull request, check run or branch.
milestones.desired_state: A contributor moves an issue, runs the gates, and CI tells them the projection is behind before a reviewer does. A person renames an issue on GitHub and the next sync updates it rather than duplicating it. A reader asks which pull request realised an issue, or which outcome a merged commit served, and one command answers from derived edges. The plan's readiness is answerable over MCP and HTTP because it is a capability, not a shell function.
non_scope: Replacing the canonical model, which is not the defect
Importing GitHub semantics into canonical records; GitHub stays a projection
Moving network calls into the tool itself, which test/cases/08_no_forbidden_constructs.sh forbids
A GraphQL client, or any provider abstraction beyond the one GitHub host this repository publishes to
Assignees, reactions, projects boards or discussions
acceptance_criteria: A gate runs the drift check on every change that can move the model or the adapter, and a drift finding fails CI naming the record and the remedy
Identity is canonical data: renaming a title on GitHub moves the mapping with it and creates no duplicate record
Reconciliation is provable offline against a fixture remote, and a fixture is refused for any mutation
The reconciliation vocabulary distinguishes never-created, deleted-remotely, edited-remotely, canonically-moved and conflicting, and each state names what would change before anything changes
A pull request is related to the issue it realises by a derived edge, and the relation is traversable in both directions
The plan's derivations are readable through the capability surface, and adding one requires no edit to a transport registry
Every claim this milestone makes about GitHub is backed by a test that runs offline against a fixture
risks: The backfill is an outward-facing mutation: applying the projection creates roughly 180 public issues in one run. It must be a deliberate, confirmed act, not a side effect of wiring a gate.
Wiring the gate before the backfill makes CI red on master until the backfill lands. The order matters and is part of the work.
