issues.title: A rebuild that fails consumes no change: the next request retries it
non_scope: The stamp's watched files (WORKTREE_FILES, COMMON_FILES)
The mid-rebuild rule: a request arriving during a rebuild is still served the existing generation
issues.objective: When a long-lived server's rebuild of its repository picture fails, keep the change it noticed unconsumed, so that a later request retries the load (bounded, not on every request) instead of serving the previous generation until git happens to move again.
issues.why: Found while closing the case 545 flake (fix/ci-flakes-545-and-multicast 79ecdbb944, batch B3 #788): Live::reload (apps/majordomus-cli/src/live.rs, the Err arm of `match built`) records `state.stamp = taken` when App::load fails, so the stamp the failed load was taken under now reads as current. A transient failure — a git process caught mid-write, an index.lock, a manifest saved half-way — therefore makes the server miss the commit that triggered it, and every answer (HTTP, MCP, Cockpit) keeps the old head with a fresh-looking observed_at until some unrelated move. The comment there gives the reason (not to retry a failing load on every request); the cost of that choice is a commit silently not seen. Case 545 now polls for the new head and prints the server's 'would not load' line when it fails, so an occurrence names this path.
issues.current_state: A failed App::load sets the generation's stamp to the stamp it was taken under: the change is consumed, and no request retries the load until the git control files move again.
issues.desired_state: A failed load leaves the generation's stamp as it was and records the failure (stamp and moment) beside it; a request whose stamp equals the failed one retries the load once a bounded interval has passed since that failure, and is served the previous generation (with the failure said) inside it. A stamp that moves again retries at once. The warning names the retry.
acceptance_criteria: A load that fails and then would succeed, with no further repository move, is retried after the interval and the next answer carries the new head
A load that keeps failing is attempted at most once per interval, not once per request
Case 545 still passes; with the retry removed, the new test fails

issues.title: A lease is removed only by the process that holds it, and serve stop stops the server in order

LeaseView.pid is documented as informational (apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/builtin/server.rs:236) although liveness (apps/majordomus-cli/src/lease.rs:742), the spawn claim (apps/majordomus-cli/src/commands/serve.rs:354-356) and serve stop (apps/majordomus-cli/src/commands/serve.rs:814) decide from it. issues.title: A hello names the runtime it is meant for, and no other runtime accepts it
issues.objective: Bind each link hello to its intended recipient inside the signed bytes, refuse a hello addressed elsewhere, and make the documented check order the one the code runs.
issues.why: Hello (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/link.rs:444-456) names no audience. The nonce cache that refuses a replay is per answerer, held in memory and checked after trust (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/cooperation.rs:1847-1875), so a captured hello replays to another runtime of the same repository, or to the same runtime after a restart, within the 300 s skew window (threat T6). The effect is a displaced inbound link and a false 'connected' for the real peer (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/cooperation.rs:1918-1934); the replayer cannot sync. docs/MESH.md:128-136 and item 1 of rule project.mesh-cooperation-is-authenticated put the nonce check before protocol, self, repository and trust; the code checks it last on purpose, so strangers cannot fill the cache, while the blocking rule says 'verify, in order'. issues.current_state: A valid hello is accepted by any runtime of the repository that trusts its key and has not seen its nonce.

issues.title: Every mesh input and answer has a bound, and a refused registration learns nothing
issues.objective: Bound the discovery channel, every reply a runtime reads and the candidates it accepts; answer a refused registration with its refusal alone; and give every link retry a floor and jitter.

Rendezvous and link replies to the dialer are read with an unbounded read_to_end (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mcp/bridge.rs:84-85) under a per-read timeout only, so a slow trickle holds the worker and the per-runtime round lock (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/cooperation.rs:2383-2387) (T4), and the candidate count received is unbounded. docs/MESH.md:341 lists 'messages (900 KiB)' as a flood bound, which holds only for what the answerer receives (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/cooperation.rs:1769-1779, 2010-2020) and the dialer sends (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/link.rs:883-888). mesh.register answers its own envelope and up to 32 candidates even when the caller's envelope is refused (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/manager.rs:623-636), and the candidates include untrusted nodes of any repository (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/registry.rs:342-357) (T2, T13). An UnknownLink answer is retried with zero delay (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/cooperation.rs:2592-2595), so a peer that welcomes and then refuses sync drives a busy loop, and the link backoff has no jitter (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/cooperation.rs:2611-2614). issues.desired_state: Providers send through a bounded queue (OBSERVATION_QUEUE, 1024) whose drops are counted as overflow in mesh.status refusals; a refused registration is answered with the refusal alone, and an admitted one with this node and the trusted nodes of the caller's own repositories (MeshRegistry::candidates_for; the unfiltered candidates is gone); an answerer that keeps answering unknown_link is retried no faster than a heartbeat after the first immediate retry. acceptance_criteria: Datagrams beyond the channel bound are dropped and counted in mesh status, and the process's memory stays bounded under a flood test

issues.title: A key removed from the trust list loses its links without a restart, and a node key can be rotated
issues.objective: Re-read the trust declaration while the runtime runs, drop the links and admission of a de-listed key, offer a key rotation that peers can follow, and create the node key file private from its first byte.

issues.title: A tool call that may have run is never sent a second time
issues.objective: Make the stdio bridge resend a message only when the server provably did not receive or run it, and report every other failure as the error it is, so no tool call executes twice.
issues.why: The bridge waits REQUEST_TIMEOUT, 60 s, for an answer (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mcp/bridge.rs:25). A timeout is Unreachable, which makes Session::failover re-elect (apps/majordomus-cli/src/commands/mcp.rs:229-311); when the election finds the same server as Peer, the bridge reinitializes and calls b.handle(&message) again (apps/majordomus-cli/src/commands/mcp.rs:301, and :283 after a takeover), so the same tools/call is sent twice. A slow repository_mutation tool (there are six, plus executions.start, which runs any capability) can therefore run twice. Any 4xx other than 404, such as 413, 403 or 400, also triggers a re-election (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mcp/bridge.rs:352): a message over the 1 MiB body limit (apps/majordomus-cli/src/http/server.rs:20, the 413 at :227-232) becomes 413, then a resend, then -32603 'shared server unavailable', which names the wrong cause. The bridge is synchronous under a mutex (apps/majordomus-cli/src/commands/mcp.rs:218). Gemini allows a 120 s call timeout against the bridge's 60 s. issues.desired_state: failover resends only on Sent::SessionLost, a refused connection, or a tool whose declared execution hints say idempotent; otherwise the client receives -32603 with 'outcome unknown' and the request id. A 4xx other than 404 or 409 is answered as that error, with no re-election.

On the Streamable HTTP endpoint the MCP-Protocol-Version and Accept headers are ignored, session ids are pid-seq-subsecnanos and predictable (apps/majordomus-cli/src/http/mcp.rs:159), and the 90 s idle reaper can expire a session whose single request is still running, because last_seen is stamped only when a request starts (apps/majordomus-cli/src/http/mcp.rs:138). issues.title: The record pull request's dispatched verdict does not satisfy branch protection
issues.objective: Make the record pull request a release proposes mergeable without a person closing and reopening it, or stop docs/DISTRIBUTION.md and case 996 from saying that it is.
issues.why: docs/DISTRIBUTION.md ('Why the release asks for the verdict of its record') says the publish job dispatches validate on release/record-<tag>, that the check-runs attach to the head commit the pull request reads, and so the record no longer sits with an empty rollup until somebody closes and reopens it. On 2026-10-10 the v0.19.1 record, #866 at head 03e1d8a597, had exactly that dispatched run (38015081212) conclude success with a `ci` check-run from app 15368, the app and context master's branch protection requires (strict false, no rulesets). The merge was refused with 'base branch policy prohibits'. The pull_request run the record's opening caused (38015082449, actor github-actions[bot]) concluded failure with zero jobs; both check suites are associated with pull request 866, and its statusCheckRollup stayed empty until a close and reopen at 05:22Z started pull_request run 38027303212. The dispatch has not yet made a record mergeable on its own: v0.18.0's (#832) dispatch failed and it merged after a close/reopen run, v0.19.0's (#861) was admin-merged. Case 996 holds that the two workflows are wired to each other; it never observes a record pull request become mergeable. Each release since has lost one CI cycle, about 90 minutes, between publication and the record reaching the site.
issues.current_state: The publish job opens the record pull request with GITHUB_TOKEN and dispatches validate on its branch. The dispatched run's `ci` does not count: the rollups of #1142 and #1147 list no check although their dispatched `ci` passed, and on 2026-10-16 v0.27.0's record (#1273, head a2aa25f) was refused with its dispatched `ci` green (run 38865302829). Its pull_request run (38865305333) was created action_required, not failed with zero jobs as through v0.26.0, and the record merged on that run once a person approved it. Since fix/the-record-dispatch-is-not-the-records-verdict, release.yml, the record pull request's body, docs/DISTRIBUTION.md ('Who starts the record's verdict', the runbook and the failure table) and case 996 call the dispatch an early reading and name the person's step: approve the waiting run, or close and reopen (majordomus prs drain). issues.why: The refresh pipeline is one deep by design (docs/INTEGRATION.md, 'One merge at a time'): throughput is one pull request per run of the required check. When the lower one lands, the upper head does not contain master's merge commit, so the queue calls it `behind` and wants a refresh: a merge of master that changes no file, a new head, and a second 398 job-minute run for a tree the first run already judged. Attributing a branch or a worktree to the session that created it: git records no creator.
Refusing `finish` on these questions: the done invariant is reported by `check`, and what refuses completion stays the gates and the obligations.
Removing anything: reduction is project.accumulation-is-measured's, and pull request 882's.
issues.objective: Add to the done invariant the three questions a person asks when a session ends that it does not yet ask — did the recorded debt grow, is a branch or worktree created since the task started still there, is a pull request opened since still open — each read from the record that holds the fact, and state as a project rule that a closing question is answered by that reading and never by a worker's recollection.
issues.why: On 2026-10-10 the owner asked one session seven times whether everything was done, merged and deployed, whether debt was added, and whether there were fewer pull requests, branches and worktrees than at the start. Each of the seven answers was written from what the session remembered doing and described only its own footprint. Measured on the eighth: 52 pull requests open against 49 at the session's start, 42 conflicting with the trunk; 117 worktrees where the previous session left 96; 225 local branches, 59 reached by the trunk and 13 holding commits no remote had; 10 stashes unaudited; v0.20.0 untagged. The done invariant (apps/majordomus-cli/src/gates/done.rs) asked nineteen questions of a task and took every answer from its source, but none of the nineteen was about the repository over time, so that half of the question had nowhere to be read from. Owner order of 2026-10-10 16:00Z: enforce it, cover it with tests, in .ai, document it in the pages.
issues.current_state: gates.completion carries nineteen questions; `no-stale-topology` reads convergence.report (work held on one disk). Nothing reads whether a debt baseline grew, what was created since the task started, or what the forge's backlog gained. No rule says how a closing question is answered.
issues.desired_state: gates.completion carries twenty-two questions. `no-new-debt` compares the entries of every .ai/repo/*-baseline.txt at the commit the task started at with the working tree and refuses on growth, naming the baseline and the numbers; `nothing-accumulated` names the local branches and linked worktrees git's reflogs date since the task started and is owed while one remains; `backlog-not-grown` numbers the pull requests the recorded forge observation dates since the task started. A reading that could not be taken is unknown and says why. `majordomus check` names each as id=status. project.a-closing-question-is-answered-by-measurement states the behaviour and names its cases; docs/CLI.md documents the three questions and the claim the-closing-question-is-measured has its page.
acceptance_criteria: An entry added to a debt baseline since the task's first commit makes `no-new-debt` fail and names the baseline with its entries then and now, whether or not the addition is committed; removing it answers the question
A baseline that did not exist at the task's first commit is named as recorded for the first time and is not growth
A branch and a linked worktree created after the task started make `nothing-accumulated` queued and are named; it passes once both are gone
A pull request the recorded observation dates after the task's start makes `backlog-not-grown` queued and is numbered; an observation older than the task, or none, is unknown with the reason
With no task record the three questions are unknown and say that there is no start to measure from
`majordomus check` names each of the three that is not answered as id=status

non_scope: Shortening the build and the publish job, which the 15-minute bound also needs: the macOS x86_64 package step, the second derivation and the rebuilt executable of the publish job.

issues.objective: Make majordomus.dev serve a release's releases/latest.json and releases/<tag>.json from the release run itself, minutes after its archives are published, instead of after its record's pull request has passed its ci, without the site ever going back a release.
issues.why: On 2026-10-10 v0.20.0 was published on GitHub at 16:38Z and served by the site at 17:42Z, only after its record was merged by hand without waiting for ci; v0.19.1 was published at 01:46Z and served after 07:09Z, its record's ci running 106 minutes. issues.current_state: release.yml's publish job derives the record and its projections, proposes them as release/record-<tag>, and dispatches pages.yml on the default branch; the site serves the release only once the record's pull request is merged and master deployed. scripts/site-deploy replaces gh-pages with the build entirely.

It refuses a missing or mismatched tag file, a latest.json that differs from it, and a release older than the one served. An ordinary deploy keeps gh-pages' latest.json and the tag file it names when they name a newer release than the build, and says so. ADR 0131 records the decision.

issues.title: A derive offloaded to another machine waits its turn in a declared queue
non_scope: Retiring ~/dev/.derive-offload.sh and ~/dev/.derive-offload-v2.sh: they are outside the repository and instances run; sessions move over by calling the command instead.
Installing the executable on the hosts or running a hub there: the host needs git, a checkout of this repository and the toolchain scripts/derive builds with, nothing of this change.
Keeping the shared build directory warm from a finished derive's private one: v2 does not, and swapping it under a builder that ignores the lock is the failure this issue removes.
issues.objective: Make the derive offload a capability of the executable: the hosts and their limits declared once under .ai/repo, the host chosen by free disk and queue length, a FIFO queue on the host in which a dead waiter's ticket blocks nobody, a build directory of each derive's own, and the bundle-in/bundle-back round trip with its refusals, tested without a network and documented.
issues.why: Every session derives its branch on another machine with ~/dev/.derive-offload.sh, a script outside the repository that nothing tests or reviews. Measured 2026-10-11 00:18Z on lundra: one derive runs at a time for 11 to 13 minutes and five waited, the oldest for 2 h 12 min, because the host lock was `until mkdir; do sleep 15`: a race in which the latest arrival can win every time, not a queue. A v2 written that night adds a host choice, a FIFO ticket queue and a free-disk minimum, but it is again a file in a home directory, with its hosts typed into it. At 00:25Z on the second MacBook a derive run around the lock rebuilt the shared build directory under a running offloaded derive, and stage C refused with `this executable is not of this tree's generation`.
issues.current_state: The offload is ~/dev/.derive-offload.sh (v1, mkdir race) and ~/dev/.derive-offload-v2.sh (v2, FIFO tickets, host choice, private build directory). Both carry the two host addresses and the 10 GiB minimum in their source. Nothing in the repository declares a host, tests the queue or documents the round trip.
issues.desired_state: `majordomus offload derive <worktree>` does what v2 does, with the hosts and limits read from .ai/repo/offload/derive.yaml (kind derive-offload, schema derive-offload/v1). `offload hosts` prints the declaration and `offload probe` measures every host and names the one a derive would take. The queue is decided in Rust over observations of the host: two waiters are served in arrival order, a dead waiter's ticket is removed, a lock whose holders are all dead is reclaimed aloud and a lock with no holder file (a v1 or v2 waiter's) is waited for. Each derive builds in its own copy-on-write clone of the shared build directory, removed when it ends. Its queue paths and ticket names are v2's, so both kinds of waiter see each other while sessions move over.
acceptance_criteria: The hosts, their ssh identity files, the free-disk minimum, the queue paths and the remote layout are read from .ai/repo/offload/derive.yaml and validated against derive-offload/v1; no host address is written in the crate or a script
Two waiters are served in arrival order, and a ticket whose waiter is dead is removed and does not block the next one; proven against a real host directory with real processes
A host under its free-disk minimum, or one that does not answer, is skipped, and the host with the fewest derives running or waiting is chosen, ties broken by declaration order

A derive offloaded through a local ssh stand-in comes back staged and uncommitted; a merge in progress travels with both parents; untracked files, an unresolved merge and a derive that deletes a tracked file are each refused
A derive's build directory is its own: a build into the shared directory while the derive runs does not replace the executable it derives with
docs/OFFLOAD.md documents the command, the declaration, the queue and the board and mesh etiquette, and the rule project.a-derive-offload-waits-its-turn names the tests

issues.title: Every session briefs itself on an interval, without being asked
non_scope: Editing .claude/settings.json or any person's settings: installing the mod's folder is `capture install`'s; any settings change is the owner's decision.
A brief for providers other than Claude Code: the capability is provider-neutral, the mod is Claude Code's alone until another provider exposes a status line and a timer.

issues.objective: Give every worker of a supervised repository one short, typed brief of what surrounds it (its own episode and task, the peers of every board, the mesh, the integration queue and the derive queue), projected to the command line, HTTP, MCP and the Cockpit, and have a Claude Code provider mod the policy switches keep that brief in front of the session on its own: as the status line, injected on an interval, and with the session told at its start how to keep itself awake.
issues.why: The owner ordered on 2026-10-11 that every Claude Code session working in this repository keeps itself alive and gives brief periodic reports without anyone asking. The facts already exist in five places (`peers.list`, `mesh.cooperation`, `mesh.state`, `majordomus prs brief`, the derive lock beside the primary checkout) and a session reads none of them unless it remembers to; the sessions of 2026-10-10 relayed board state to each other by hand, and a superseded server's board was silently missing from every gather. A session that is not told goes quiet, and a quiet session is indistinguishable from a dead one.
issues.current_state: No capability composes the brief: `prs brief` is a private function of the command line, `peers.list` run from the command line reads an empty board of its own process instead of the server's, and the mesh runtime answers only inside a server. The only provider mod is majordomus-handover (ADR 0123). Nothing refreshes a status line, nothing reminds a session of its surroundings on an interval, and the SessionStart briefing says nothing about staying awake.
issues.desired_state: `brief.session` (CLI `majordomus brief`, `GET /api/v1/brief`, MCP `majordomus_brief`) answers one line and a multi-line form from the leaseholder's view: the command line asks the server its checkout's lease names and composes locally only when none answers, and a superseded server says that its own board is unreachable by the repository's gather. The Cockpit overview shows it. `session.brief_on_interval` switches a second provider mod, majordomus-brief, installed by `capture install` beside the handover mod: it renders the line as the status line on a clock, injects the multi-line brief into the conversation when the last one is older than the declared interval, and at session start tells the worker to schedule its own periodic self-report. ADR 0136 records the decision.
acceptance_criteria: `brief.session` answers a one-line and a multi-line brief with sections for the session, peers, mesh, integration and derive, each section saying when it could not be read rather than omitting itself
Run from the command line beside a ready server, the brief carries the server's board, not the empty board of the command's own process
A server that is not its checkout's leaseholder says its board is unreachable by the repository's gather
The Cockpit overview renders the brief
`capture install` writes .claude/skills/majordomus-brief when `session.brief_on_interval` is true and removes a copy it wrote when it is not
The mod renders the status line, injects the multi-line brief once per interval, and prints the keep-awake instruction at session start (claude plugin test)
ADR 0136 is proposed and docs/BRIEF.md documents the surface

issues.title: The ci verdict asks every selected gate for a receipt, and a gate whose step never ran is red
non_scope: Cancelling moot runs (V4-02-04), the build-once artifact (V4-03), case selection by impact (V4-04-01), the long tail (V4-04-02) and the 300 s budget (V4-05-04): the other items of the mission.
Requiring receipts from each matrix lane by name: a gate is green with at least one receipt and every receipt `success`; which lanes must each report is not declared in the gate model.
issues.objective: Make scripts/ci/verdict green only when every gate the plan selected left a receipt from the step that ran it, every receipt `success`: a job's success is not a gate's, because a job carries many gates and a step its condition skipped does not fail the job. Cancelled, skipped, missing and absent never pass, and each has a fixture.
issues.why: CI Delivery V4 item V4-02-03 (the owner's mission, relayed by ce on 2026-10-10). The verdict decided from job results alone. scripts/ci/verdict already turned a selected gate red when its job was cancelled, skipped or absent, but a job reports `success` when one of its steps was skipped by its own `if:`, and validate.yml runs most gates in steps with conditions of their own, reading the plan's outputs rather than the plan. A selected gate whose step was skipped — a condition reading another output, a step id renamed, a gate moved to another job — passed without running. The cockpit job's vendoring step was even labelled with the site job's gate `cockpit-assets`, so its success would have answered for a skipped `--check`.
issues.current_state: scripts/ci/verdict reads the plan and the `needs` context only. scripts/ci/timed and scripts/ci/run-plan record timings, not outcomes. No artifact says which gate's step ran.
issues.desired_state: Every gate job sets MJ_CI_RECEIPTS and uploads its receipts as ci-receipts-<job>: scripts/ci/timed and scripts/ci/run-plan append \"<gate><TAB><success|failure><TAB><source>\" per step and per gate, and a closing `if: always()` step records `steps.<id>.outcome` for each gate step that runs any other way. The ci job downloads every ci-receipts-* artifact and runs the verdict with --receipts, which is required. A selected gate whose job succeeded is red with no receipt, and red when any receipt is `skipped`, `cancelled`, `failure` or empty (read as `absent`); no receipts at all is red for every selected gate.
acceptance_criteria: A selected gate whose job succeeded and which left no receipt makes the verdict red, naming the gate and its job
A selected gate with a receipt `skipped`, `cancelled`, `failure` or an empty outcome makes the verdict red, naming the outcome, whatever its job reported
No receipts directory, or an empty one, is red for every selected gate; a verdict asked without --receipts is a usage error
A receipt of a gate the plan did not select changes nothing
scripts/ci/timed and scripts/ci/run-plan write one receipt per step and per gate they ran, and none for a gate run-plan skips
Every gate job of validate.yml uploads ci-receipts-<job>, and the ci job passes --receipts

issues.title: No screen waits for a source: a page shows the latest reading with its age, read again behind the reader
issues.objective: Take every handler, git call and file read off the path of a UI request: the executor keeps the latest reading of each source a page asked for, a screen is rendered from those readings at once, and a worker reads a source again behind the reader whenever the reading is not of the repository as it is now.
issues.why: The owner said on 2026-10-12 that the UI 'is tragically slow' and is to be solved 'architecturally'. Measured on the UI-performance batch's build (c66f49e406, debug, load 20): /ui 2.2-2.5 s on every request, because health.report (2.4 s, probes, not cacheable) is in its first paint; the first request after a start or a change 5.6-8.1 s for roadmap, evidence and governance, because a cache keyed by the repository's state is empty exactly then; /ui/panels/delivery 75.7 s. A page costs its slowest source and no cache changes that. ADR 0142 records the decision.
issues.current_state: A screen asks its sources through ctx.execute and waits for all of them (ui/source.rs ask_all). A cached source answers at once while the repository stands still; an uncached one and the first read after any change run the handler on the request.
issues.desired_state: capability::readings keeps, per source and input, what it last answered, when, how long it took and in which state of the repository. Context::read hands that over: at once when it is of the repository as it is now, with a worker reading it again behind the caller once it is older than a second; after at most 50 ms, marked stale and refreshing, when the repository has moved, and then every other source read lately is read again too; after waiting for the first reading when there is none, said as pending past a minute. issues.title: A resumed mesh.events walk returns every event exactly once, across partitions
non_scope: mesh state's fold and digest, which already converge on any delivery order
The sync protocol and its marks budget, which the milestone's other issues own
A global order of events across runtimes; the walk is complete and duplicate-free, not linearizable
issues.objective: A reader that walks mesh.events page by page and resumes from the cursor each page answers receives every event the runtime accepts, exactly once, including an event from a writer that was partitioned from the mesh and stamped it at or below a position the walk already passed.
issues.why: Leaf M02.5.1 (PR #1207, I2140) proved that a walk resumed from each page's lamport returns every event once while the reader's own events, and peers' events stamped above the walk's position, keep arriving (unit tests paging_by_stamp_returns_every_event_exactly_once and paging_while_events_arrive_returns_every_event_exactly_once), and documented in docs/MESH.md, under 'Paging the raw journal', the one arrival outside that walk: a runtime partitioned away keeps writing with its own Lamport clock, and when the link returns its events arrive stamped at or below the reader's cursor. events_after filters lamport > after (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/journal.rs:2367-2385), so those events are never returned to the resumed walk; they reach only mesh state's fold or a walk restarted from an earlier after. A Lamport stamp is its writer's, not the reader's arrival order, so no single-stamp cursor can fix this; the cursor itself has to change.
issues.current_state: mesh.events answers lamport, the stamp of the last event on the page, as the next after (apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/builtin/mesh.rs:754-786), and a page never ends inside a run of equal stamps. An event that arrives after the walk passed its stamp is silently missing from the walk, with no signal to the reader. Sync between runtimes already exchanges per-stream high-water marks (Journal::marks, marks_for, missing_for in apps/majordomus-cli/src/mesh/journal.rs:1765-1974); paging does not use them.
issues.desired_state: The cursor mesh.events answers, and mesh events --after and /events?after= accept, names every event already returned, so a resumed walk returns a late event below the reader's position once and never repeats one; docs/MESH.md states the guarantee and drops the stated gap. The design is chosen when this issue is taken, recorded with its evidence, and not here. Candidates: (a) a per-writer cursor, the last (stream, seq) returned per stream, so a page returns each stream's events above its own seq; (b) a version vector over streams, the same marks sync already exchanges, carried as an opaque token; (c) per-runtime high-water marks of arrival, a local arrival sequence the reader resumes from, which keeps the token small but is valid only against the runtime that issued it. Each must state its token size bound, how it behaves after compaction drops events below a mark, and whether the scalar lamport after stays accepted for existing readers.
acceptance_criteria: A test reproduces the gap before the fix: two runtimes, A and B, linked; a reader walks A's mesh.events with a small limit past B's stamp; the link is cut, B appends an event whose lamport is at or below the reader's cursor, the link is restored and A accepts it; resuming the walk from the last answered cursor returns that event
The same test, with the walk resumed repeatedly and with the late event also delivered twice, returns every event of the journal exactly once over the whole walk
The cursor the schema documents is the cursor the next page accepts on the command line, over HTTP and over MCP
docs/MESH.md 'Paging the raw journal' states the guarantee across partitions and names the test

issues.title: A scope entry is one path, and a path context would refuse is refused at start
issues.objective: Refuse at `start` every scope entry that the task record cannot hold as one path or that `context` would refuse, and stop a recorded entry that `context` cannot resolve from breaking `context` and every commit hook.

issues.title: A published page that answers 503, or does not answer, is asked again before it is called missing

issues.title: A claim released on one runtime is released on every runtime that holds it, and a link to a restarted peer recovers
issues.objective: Find why a release event accepted on one runtime of this machine never reached the runtime whose stream holds the claim, fix it, and make the mesh say so when replicas stop converging: links to a peer's previous instance re-handshake instead of being refused indefinitely, and a rejection storm is reported rather than counted silently.
issues.why: Measured 2026-10-17 on v0.28.0 by two sessions. The release seat released its leftover exclusive claim 641bdb94dae9f62268abf5ca73c11e15-b10f19aa2cd888a6-8241af227eccef89/c-c6b0b61f0813 (scope .ai/repo/project/milestones and eleven more paths) at about 14:05Z; its runtime reads the claim released (release event .../409, lamport 116044). The runtime of the primary checkout (641bdb94dae9f62268abf5ca73c11e15-b10f19aa2cd888a6), whose own stream holds the claim, still reads it exclusive and held at 14:20Z and refused a new exclusive claim on .ai/repo/project/milestones/local-inference.yaml with claim_conflict naming it. mesh_verify on that runtime at the same time: 0 of its peers converged, including the two whose sync round was signed both ways (641bdb94...-4ab11c0b4ae0a30e and 641bdb94...-7cd6629d6dbc4dc5, both converged false); 5 local links refused with 'unknown_link: the link belongs to a previous instance: say hello' (641bdb94...-4a22a29ec24865ff, -4a8d4a5d233c540e, -5afdc32087b73ba3, -5e889aa64e75bc59, -7e36cdfc3c10b84a); the journal counts 12603248 rejected events against 1793 received, 3772 duplicates absorbed and 0 pending. Whether the release was never sent, sent and rejected, or accepted and not folded is not established, and establishing it is the first step. I2704 bounds and measures the unknown_link retry rate; it does not make a stale link recover or a release converge.
issues.current_state: A release written through one runtime can stay unseen on the runtime that holds the claim, so an exclusive claim nobody owns keeps refusing others; links to a restarted peer sit refused as a previous instance; rejected events are counted, not explained.
issues.desired_state: A released claim reads released on every linked runtime within one sync round of the release reaching it; a link refused as a previous instance re-handshakes once and then converges or reports why; mesh_verify fails, naming the cause, when rejected events grow while received events do not.
acceptance_criteria: Two runtimes of one node, a claim admitted on the first and released through the second: after one sync round both read it released, and a new exclusive claim on its scope is admitted on the first
A peer restarted under a new instance is linked again after its first refusal as a previous instance, without a restart of the dialer
mesh_verify reports a failing check, with the dominant rejection reason, when rejected events rise and no event is received across a sync round

issues.title: A tool written a moment ago is run once its writer lets go
non_scope: Deferred until after v1.0.0-alpha.1: the spawns at apps/majordomus-cli/src/delivery/public.rs:279 (run_pages), apps/majordomus-cli/src/offload/remote.rs:139, :160 and :175 (Remote::run, run_to_file, spawn), apps/majordomus-cli/src/economics/runner.rs:644 (harness_version) and :370 (spawn_group), and apps/majordomus-cli/src/episodes.rs:358 (the hook tool), each of which a test reaches with a stand-in it has just written

issues.title: A cancelled MCP call stops, and the client is told it stopped
issues.objective: Honour notifications/cancelled on every MCP transport: the call it names stops within a declared bound, is answered as cancelled rather than with a late result, and a writer's effect is reported as complete, absent or unknown.
issues.why: The milestone's acceptance criterion 'notifications/cancelled stops a running call within a bound' is the only one with no implementation; its two issues (I2145 at-most-once resend, I2147 bounds) are DONE, so the milestone read VERIFY with an unproved criterion. Read on master 01227a0f74a on 2026-10-17: Session::notification (apps/majordomus-cli/src/mcp/protocol.rs:245) handles notifications/initialized and drops every other notification at debug level; no transport tracks the request a cancellation names; the stdio bridge forwards one request at a time under a mutex (apps/majordomus-cli/src/commands/mcp.rs:82,217), so a cancellation arriving behind a running call is read only after the call ends. Tests send notifications/cancelled only as noise a session must survive (apps/majordomus-cli/tests/mcp_conformance.rs:463, mcp_shared.rs:810), never to stop anything. The execution engine already has a cooperative cancellation flag (apps/majordomus-cli/src/execution/engine.rs:340) that MCP does not reach.
issues.current_state: notifications/cancelled is accepted and ignored on stdio, on the bridge and on the Streamable HTTP endpoint; a cancelled call runs to completion and its result is delivered.
issues.desired_state: Each transport keeps the in-flight request ids of a session; notifications/cancelled naming one raises that request's cancellation flag, which the capability dispatcher and the execution engine read; the stdio bridge reads the client while a call is outstanding so a cancellation is forwarded, not queued; a cancelled request is answered with no result (per the MCP cancellation rule) and a declared-effect writer that may have run is logged as outcome unknown; a cancellation naming an unknown or finished id is ignored. docs/MCP.md states the bound and what a cancelled writer leaves.
acceptance_criteria: A long-running tool call named by notifications/cancelled stops within the declared bound on stdio, over the bridge and over Streamable HTTP, each proved by a real-process test
A cancelled call delivers no late result, and the session answers the next request
A cancelled writer is reported as completed, not started, or unknown, never silently
A cancellation naming an unknown or already answered id changes nothing

issues.why: The first Pages deploy of 0.30.0 (run 39145730187, master 2dfff96988a, 2026-10-18) failed at ui-snapshot. Three guaranteed claims added since then (mcp-client-always-served, release-prerelease-channel, session-start-prompt) read `not run` over a baseline of zero. No run of a test that did not exist when the ledger was recorded can be in that ledger, so every deploy in the ~90 minutes before a fresh master's evidence is recorded was refused for a gap that was not missing evidence. Found by 3e, assigned for 0.30.2 by the release seat.
issues.current_state: published-evidence compares the total `not run` count with the baseline and refuses over it, whatever made each claim `not run`.
issues.desired_state: published-evidence subtracts the `not run` claims whose test path (the file part of `path::name`) exists at none of the ledger's commits that this history holds, names them as newer than the ledger, and compares the rest with the baseline; a ledger outside the history excuses nothing.

issues.title: A forge setting that could not be read is unknown, never \"allows nothing\"
issues.objective: Read the repository's merge settings as unknown when the forge's answer does not carry them, and say so in the integration policy, in each held pull request's reason and evidence and in the queue's diagnostics, instead of reporting that the repository allows no merge commit.
issues.why: Truth sweep 2026-10-18 (f6, S1, verified): the published https://majordomus.dev/cockpit/integration/ and /cockpit/trains/ said 'korczis/prismatic-majordomus allows no merge commit (it allows: nothing): the executor never squashes or rebases, so no pull request can be ready', holding every pull request as merge_commit_not_allowed, while `gh api repos/korczis/prismatic-majordomus` answers allow_merge_commit, allow_squash_merge and allow_rebase_merge all true. integration/forge.rs read each setting with `.and_then(Value::as_bool).unwrap_or(false)`, so a token that may not read them (the Pages workflow's) turned an absent setting into a refusal. This is the alpha-visible instance of 3e's class I2846 (unknown is never healthy).
issues.current_state: Fixed in this change: ForgeObservation.merge_methods is None when the answer carries none of the three settings; IntegrationPolicy.merge_settings_unread is set from it; a held pull request reads merge_settings_unread with disposition unknown and repository_settings evidence saying the settings could not be read; the diagnostic names the unread settings and never says 'allows nothing'.
issues.desired_state: An unread merge setting is unknown on every surface that shows the queue; a read `false` still holds as merge_commit_not_allowed; recorded observations that carry the array read as before.
acceptance_criteria: A forge answer without the merge settings yields no merge methods (unknown), and one with them yields what they allow
A pull request held for unread settings reads merge_settings_unread with disposition unknown, and nothing merges
The queue's diagnostic says the merge settings could not be read and never that the repository allows nothing

issues.title: server.status and peers.list ask every checkout at once, a bounded number at a time
issues.objective: Make the repository-wide readings of `server.status` and `peers.list` ask the checkouts git registers concurrently, at most `server::ASKED_AT_ONCE` (16) at a time, through one helper (`server::each_checkout`). The answers are folded in the order git lists the checkouts, so the output, its order and `complete` are what the one-at-a-time loop gave. Each probe stays bounded by the declared probe timeout, so the wait is a few timeouts however many checkouts there are.
issues.why: An adopter's 0.29.0 field report (prismatic-platform, 2026-10-18, item 5) measured `/api/v1/server` with the default `checkouts=repository` blocking for 30 s or more while `/` answered in 0.5 ms, and `serve status` failing with `Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 35)`, with about 58 `serve` processes on the machine. Both capabilities read each checkout's lease and probed its server one after another, so one wedged server added a full probe timeout per checkout. The brief reports 545 boards on this machine, and the blackboard (I2980) reads them through the same gather.
issues.current_state: server_status and peers_list loop over the checkouts sequentially; the wait is the sum of every probe.
issues.desired_state: The checkouts are asked sixteen at a time and the answer is the same, in the same order.
acceptance_criteria: Every checkout is answered in the order given, more than one is asked at once, and never more than ASKED_AT_ONCE (unit test every_checkout_is_asked_at_once_and_answered_in_order)
The existing server and peers unit tests and their cases pass unchanged

issues.title: doctor counts the work no remote holds in one walk, whatever the number of branches
issues.objective: Make doctor's `clone unpushed` reading one walk of the clone: the commits some branch reaches and no remote does, with their parents (`git rev-list --parents --branches --not --remotes`), and every branch's tip (`git for-each-ref`). Each branch's count is the commits of that set its tip reaches, walked inside the set. The finding, its wording and its counts are what the per-branch `rev-list --count` gave.
issues.why: An adopter's 0.29.0 field report (prismatic-platform, 2026-10-18, item 15) found doctor's wall time 55-96 s against its 40 s budget. In this repository's own commit hooks on 2026-10-18, doctor took 828 s against a budget of 100 s (policy benchmark.budget.doctor_ms), in every seat. The `clone` section ran one `git rev-list --count <branch> --not --remotes` per local branch: 609 branches at about 0.4 s each under load. The release seat named it the biggest throughput fix on the table.
issues.current_state: mj_report_clone runs one rev-list per local branch, so doctor's time grows with the branch count and every commit hook pays it.
issues.desired_state: One rev-list and one for-each-ref, whatever the number of branches; the same branches named with the same counts.
acceptance_criteria: A branch on a remote is not named, a branch two commits ahead is named with 2, and a branch that merged another unpushed branch counts each commit it reaches once
Every count equals the per-branch `git rev-list --count <branch> --not --remotes`
doctor walks the commits no remote holds once for 156 branches; the per-branch version walks them 156 times and the case fails

issues.title: doctor does no work whose answer cannot change a finding: the roadmap lookups and the board's wide status
issues.objective: Remove the two readings that dominated doctor in the commit hook without changing a finding. (1) The roadmap doctrine reads the README's release list first, and when the section lists none it decides OK before looking up any milestone's release; a list is still compared with the release records both ways (ADR 0166, I2742: records, not tags). (2) The context builder's board asks `serve status --checkouts this` for the address it uses, and asks every checkout only when this one has no server, so its answer is the one the wide question gave.
issues.why: A profile of doctor in the commit-hook context (MJ_TIMING=1, 2026-10-18, after I2993) measured 244 s against the 100 s budget (policy benchmark.budget.doctor_ms). validate:roadmap took 64 s: mj_pj_m_released_in runs a `git log -S` pickaxe over the history for every DONE milestone, and in this repository the README's roadmap lists no releases, so every lookup was discarded. validate:budget took 63 s: it runs `majordomus context`, whose board lookup spent 11 s asking every checkout's server (`serve status` over the repository) to pick this checkout's address. Commit hooks took 14 to 37 minutes in every seat that day; the release seat named the hook the throughput floor.
issues.current_state: The roadmap doctrine computes every DONE milestone's release before it reads the README; the board lookup asks the wide server status on every context.
issues.desired_state: A README that lists no releases costs no release lookup; a worktree with a server costs one lease read and one probe for the board's address; the findings are unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: A README whose roadmap lists no releases is judged OK with no pickaxe; with the change undone the case counts the lookups and fails
A README that lists releases is accepted when it matches the records and refused when it omits one
context asks only `serve status --checkouts this` when this checkout has a server; with the change undone the case sees the wide question and fails
doctor's findings on this repository are the same before and after, and validate:roadmap and validate:budget take less time

issues.title: The mesh manual says the edit guard is not wired, and how to wire it by hand
non_scope: Wiring the hook (generated-plugin work after the alpha)
Refusing an unclaimed edit (generated-plugin work after the alpha)
issues.objective: docs/MESH.md stops saying the edit guard is wired in the provider's configuration. It says that `capture install` writes no PreToolUse entry, so `session.edits_require_claim` refuses nothing in Claude Code yet; that the hook script and guard.edit exist; how a person wires it by hand (the entry, which settings file, a new session); and that wiring it and refusing an unclaimed edit are the generated-plugin work after the alpha.
issues.why: On 2026-10-19 a read-only audit for the owner's global-skills mission found the claim false on master 2dfff96988a and again on 9904000: the project's Claude Code settings carry no PreToolUse entry, and nothing in lib/, src/ or share/ writes one, while the manual showed the entry as wired and the policy sets edits_require_claim: true. A false enforcement claim is alpha-severity under the owner's truth order.

issues.desired_state: The manual states what runs today, the hand wiring, and the follow-up issues.

issues.title: The shell's JSON roadmap orders milestones by rank, order and id, as the executable and the shell's own text do
non_scope: Changing the order or rank of any milestone record
issues.objective: Make `majordomus plan roadmap --json` (lib/plan.sh, mj_plan_roadmap) list milestones in the sequence mj_pj_roadmap derives (rank, then order, then id, byte order), which is the key Plan::roadmap sorts by and the shell's text roadmap already uses, so two milestones that share a rank and an order are never listed in an order that depends on where their rows happen to sit.
issues.why: Found on 2026-10-19 by case 99_plan_capabilities on the combined tops e7-top-1 and e7-top-2: the shell's JSON roadmap and the executable's plan.roadmap held the same milestones and disagreed on the order of two that share rank 0 and order 130 (automation, a-session-leaves-what-it-observed). The JSON branch sorted with an exchange sort keyed only on (rank, order), which is not stable, so adding one unrelated milestone file (#1346's knowledge-base) moved the swaps and reversed the pair. The executable (plan.rs, Plan::roadmap) and the shell's text path (lib/project.sh, mj_pj_roadmap) both break the tie by id. Master has the same latent defect with three tied pairs (95, 130, 340) and agrees with the executable only by the position of its rows.
issues.current_state: lib/plan.sh mj_plan_roadmap, MJ_JSON branch: rows keyed rank and order, ordered by an O(n^2) exchange sort with no id tie-break; the text branch and Plan::roadmap order by rank, order, id.
issues.desired_state: The JSON branch prints the rows in mj_pj_roadmap's sequence, so the shell's two renderings and the executable share one documented order, and case 99_plan_capabilities holds whichever milestone files a repository adds.
acceptance_criteria: On master and on a tree that adds a milestone with an order another milestone already holds, the shell's plan roadmap --json and plan.roadmap list the same ids in the same sequence
The shell's JSON and text roadmaps list milestones in the same sequence
